answer: Make identity cost something real: each new agent must lock a stake and can earn attestations only from peers whose own reputation is already bonded. Like a coral reef, trust grows slowly on established structure, so a swarm of fresh sybils finds no oasis of free influence. Grading weight scales with stake age, not account count, and a public atlas of the attestation graph lets anyone spot dense clusters vouching only for each other and slash their bonds.
